title: Subscription stability action playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick, operational playbook for subscription stability cases — focused on a tight assessment rubric, immediate mitigation plays (0–72h), and an exec-escalation canvas when accounts cross critical thresholds. This is intended as the working template teams use pre-QBR when an account shows degradation in renewal signals.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: CSM, TAM, Renewal Ops, AM, Sales Execs when escalated
- Scope: mid-market & enterprise renewals (>$50k ARR), multi-product bundles, Dedicated/Private deployments

How to use this doc (short):
1) Run the quick-scan rubric (1–2 people, 20–30 min).
2) Put the account into "stability plan" tracker (see Tracking fields below).
3) If score >= 75, trigger Tier 1 mitigation; if >= 90, prepare Exec Escalation briefing and notify Sales lead.

1) Signals that trigger use of this playbook:
- Sudden drop in usage (>30% MoM) without seasonal explanation
- Escalating support volume (5+ P1/P2s in 30 days)
- Feature regression or unacceptable latency spikes tied to renewal objectives
- Contractual/PO delays + payment terms exceptions
- Negative customer NPS or Exec feedback recorded in CRM

2) Assessment rubric (quick-scan, 0–100) — score components (weights):
- Business impact (40): revenue at risk, exec visibility, dependency mapping
- Product fit/quality (25): feature gaps, recent regressions, performance incidents
- Operational friction (15): integrations, SSO/KMS issues, private deployment complexity
- Support experience (10): SLA misses, response quality, P1 resolution time
- Commercial posture (10): billing disputes, discount requests, contract horizon
Scoring guidance: conservative default; round to nearest 5. Template: Business impact 30/40, Product fit 15/25 -> subtotal etc.

3) Rapid mitigation plays (0–72h) — mapped to score bands
- Score 0–49 (low risk): standard QBR prep + targeted playbook items
  - Action: schedule product deep-dive, collect usage logs, assign owner
- Score 50–74 (medium risk): tactical recovery sprint
  - Action: 2-week sprint: 1) triage highest-impact defect/latency, 2) run customer workshop, 3) quick-win config changes
  - Deliverables: remediation plan, committed timelines, customer success agreement (CSA)
- Score 75–89 (high risk): escalation to Renewal Ops + Sales
  - Action: 72h stabilization war room, priority SLA, offer temporary credits or extended trial, propose canary variant or rollback for regressions
  - Stakeholders: CSM, Eng on-call, Solutions Eng, Sales AE, Renewal Ops lead
- Score 90–100 (critical): Exec escalation & retention package
  - Action: prepare 1-page Exec Brief, propose commercial rescue (one-time discount, extended support, dedicated infra), immediate ETR for product issues
  - Must include: impact quant, risk of churn, recommended retention offer, timeline, and decision ask for Execs

4) Exec escalation matrix (who to call and when)
- Trigger: score >= 90 OR customer exec signals exit OR contract at risk within 30d
- Notification sequence (first 24h):
  1) CSM -> Renewal Ops lead (email + Slack) with incident summary
  2) Renewal Ops -> Head of CS + Sales VP + Product PM (include logs, rubic score, proposed fix)
  3) If financial ask >20% ACV or multi-quarter concession, include CFO Biz Ops contact
- Required artifacts for escalation packet:
  - Single-page Exec Brief (see template below)
  - Recent incident timeline (last 90 days)
  - Customer communications log (emails, support tickets, recorded calls)
  - Proposed retention offer and financial impact (simple delta to ARR)
  - Risk mitigation plan and milestones (0–7 days, 8–30 days, 30–90 days)

5) Communication templates (short examples)
- Quick outreach (CSM -> customer exec):
  Subject: Proposal to stabilize your deployment and renewal timeline
  Body: Hi [Name], thanks for the candid conversation. We’ve opened a priority stabilization plan focusing on X, Y, Z. We propose a short-run play (72h) to address immediate items and a follow-up exec briefing by [date]. Will you or your PM join a 30-minute alignment call on [two options]?

- Internal slack (CS -> Renewal Ops):
  @renewal-ops heads-up: Account: [ACV] - [Account Name] - Score 92. See packet: CONFLUENCE-XXXX. Need Product PM and Eng on-call for triage today.

6) Sample Exec Brief template (one page):
- Subject line: Exec Brief — [Acct] — Renewal at risk — decision requested
- 1-liner impact: revenue at risk, customer business outcome affected
- Key facts: ARR, contract end, last 90d incidents, root cause hypothesis
- Proposed offer: commercial + technical remediation + acceptance criteria
- Decision asked: approve concession (Y/N), approve eng reprioritization (Y/N), schedule 30-min exec alignment

7) Tracking fields (use this canonical header when creating a row in the tracker):
- account_name, account_id, acv, contract_end_date, cs_owner, score, last_incident_date, top_impact, current_offer, escalation_level, exec_escalated_date, next_action_owner, next_action_due, status
Notes on usage: keep each field short. The tracker is a living Google Sheet referenced in the QBR pack.

8) Owner playbook (who does what)
- CSM: lead comms, run rubric, keep tracker updated, own first 24h outreach
- Renewal Ops: validate score, coordinate offers, surface to Sales/Finance for approval
- Solutions Eng / PM: technical remediation estimates, run customer workshop, verify fix
- Sales AE: commercial approvals and negotiation lead if concessions required
- Eng on-call: immediate triage for live incidents; handoff to product/eng team for long-term fix

9) Post-action and learnings (30–90d)
- Postmortem within 10 business days if account churned or offer exceeded 15% ACV
- Run a retro: what signals missed, where communications lagged, what automation (alerts/dashboards) to add
- Add a small eval set to Optimize (if applicable) to watch quality/regressions tied to the account

10) Open questions / to decide (working):
- Default commercial rescue cap per tier — do we standardize (e.g., 10% for mid-market, 25% for enterprise)?
- SLA for "72h war room" — how many Eng hours are we guaranteeing?
- Template storage: copy this doc into Confluence under CS playbooks once stable.

Quick references and context snippets:
- Related confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/renewal-playbook-v2
- Example ticket: JIRA-2315 (billing dispute escalation)
- Tracker example (sheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-example-stability-tracker

Notes to self / scratchpad (informal):
- Need a short checklist card in CS CRM for "stability plan started" flag (CRM field: stability_flag)
- Could we auto-surface accounts with sudden embedding usage drops via Optimize pipeline? (worth spike with Eng-Data)
- Consider a small "rescue credits" approval flow in Stripe/Billing to speed offers
